description: Systematic Taxonomy of Psychometric Traps in GATE DA

formula_substitution_trap.description: Blindly applying a memorized formula without checking if the question's conditions match
examples: Using MSE formula when question explicitly states MAE (2026 Q55)
Using average-case QuickSort O(n log n) when pivot is fixed as first element (2026 Q15)
Using standard eigenvalue formula instead of trace/det shortcut
formula_substitution_trap.countermeasure: READ the question fully. Verify every assumption matches the formula's preconditions.

definition_trap.description: Confusing similar-sounding definitions or using colloquial understanding instead of formal definition
examples: Thinking Ridge drives weights to zero (Lasso does)
Confusing admissible vs consistent heuristic
Thinking 'orthonormal basis is unique' (false - not unique, but vectors are LI)
Confusing conditional independence with marginal independence
definition_trap.countermeasure: Know precise mathematical definitions. Distinguish: necessary vs sufficient conditions.

sign_trap.description: Sign errors in derivatives, eigenvalues, or algebraic manipulations
examples: Gradient descent: w_new = w - η∇L (not +)
Covariance: E[XY] - E[X]E[Y] (not +)
Rotation matrix: cos -sin; sin cos (sign pattern)
sign_trap.countermeasure: Calculate twice on scribble pad. Verify sign convention for each formula.

quantifier_trap.description: Misinterpreting universal vs existential quantifiers, or quantifier scope
examples: ∀x (King(x) ∧ Person(x)) vs ∀x (King(x) → Person(x)) (2025 Q15, 2026 Q14)
∃x P(x) ⇒ ∀x P(x) is NOT valid (2026 Q48)
quantifier_trap.countermeasure: Translate to English explicitly. 'All kings are persons' = ∀x (King(x) → Person(x)).

boundary_condition_trap.description: Ignoring boundary conditions in optimization, integration limits, or closed intervals
examples: Optimization on closed interval: must check endpoints (2025 Q49)
Integration limits for joint PDF with dependent bounds (0<y<x) (2024 Q56, Q59)
Binary search: ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉ not ⌈log₂ n⌉
boundary_condition_trap.countermeasure: Always check: closed interval? dependent bounds? inclusive/exclusive?

examples: Which is NOT true? Which is FALSE? (2024 Q24, 2025 Q28, 2026 Q14)
Maximum variance direction vs minimum
Number of support vectors vs margin value
interpretation_trap.countermeasure: Circle/underline negation words. Re-read question before final answer.

multi_concept_trap.description: Question spans multiple domains; candidate only sees one domain
examples: Probability + Linear Algebra: X=aZ+b, find a,b from E[X], Var(X), Cov(X,Z) (2025 Q20)
ML + Calculus: Backprop through ReLU (2025 Q42, 2026 Q29)
DBMS + Algorithms: Push selection down before join (2026 Q42)
multi_concept_trap.countermeasure: Identify ALL domains involved. Solve each component then combine.

computational_trap.description: Excessive computation when a property/shortcut exists
examples: Computing M^2026 via multiplication instead of M^5=I periodicity (2026 Q21)
Computing full characteristic polynomial instead of trace/det (2025 Q28)
Full backprop through dead ReLU neuron (2025 Q42)
computational_trap.countermeasure: STOP. Recognize pattern. Use property: periodicity, rank-1, dead neuron, projection matrix.

time_trap.description: Question designed to consume excessive time; low marks/minute
examples: Complex recursive Python tracing (2025 Q47, 2026 Q39, Q58)
B+ tree insertion with splits (2026 Q41)
Large game tree minimax (2025 Q43)
time_trap.countermeasure: Set 3-minute limit for 2-mark MCQ. If exceeded, MARK and SKIP. Return in review phase.

negative_marking_trap.description: Guessing on MCQs with low confidence, losing net marks
examples: 1-mark MCQ: -1/3 for wrong; need ≥70% confidence to attempt
2-mark MCQ: -2/3 for wrong; need ≥60% confidence to attempt
MSQ/NAT: NO negative marking → ALWAYS attempt
negative_marking_trap.countermeasure: Strict confidence thresholds. Never guess blindly on MCQs.

msq_completeness_trap.description: Selecting only some correct options in MSQ (all-or-nothing marking)
examples: 2025 Q28 (I+xx^T): Must select BOTH (A) and (B); selecting one = 0 marks
2026 Q52 (centering): Must select BOTH (A) and (D)
msq_completeness_trap.countermeasure: Treat EACH option as independent True/False. Prove/disprove each separately. If unsure on one, don't select it.

notation_panic_trap.description: Dense mathematical notation (I - 1/n 11^T, ΣΣ, ∇²) causes freeze response
examples: 2026 Q52: M = I - (1/n)11^T - looks complex but is standard centering matrix
2026 Q44: Var((2X-1)Y) - expand using independence
2025 Q38: Gram matrix Aij = xi^T xj - positive definite if LI
notation_panic_trap.countermeasure: Recognize STANDARD NOTATION PATTERNS. I - 1/n 11^T = centering. xx^T = rank-1. xi^T xj = Gram.
